title: Graphing Tangent, Cotangent, Secant, and Cosecant

PF2-F-01.hint: Tangent is sine over cosine and cotangent is cosine over sine, so each is undefined where its denominator is \(0\). Set the inside of the function equal to the first excluded angle plus a multiple of the period, then solve for \(x\). The period of \(\tan(kx)\) and \(\cot(kx)\) is \(\dfrac{\pi}{|k|}\). For the range, ask whether the outputs of tangent and cotangent are limited to an interval.
slips: Using \(2\pi\) as the period of tangent or cotangent. Their basic period is \(\pi\).
Setting the inside of the function equal to an excluded angle but forgetting to divide by \(k\) when solving for \(x\).
Giving a restricted range such as \([-1, 1]\), which belongs to sine and cosine. Check whether tangent and cotangent outputs are limited.

PF2-F-02.hint: Secant is \(\dfrac{1}{\cos}\) and cosecant is \(\dfrac{1}{\sin}\), so each is undefined where that cosine or sine is \(0\). For a stretch factor \(a\), start from the fact that sine and cosine stay between \(-1\) and \(1\), then ask what taking the reciprocal does to those values. The basic period is \(2\pi\), divided by \(|k|\).
slips: Giving \([-a, a]\) or all real numbers as the range. Pick a value inside \([-a, a]\) and ask whether the graph can reach it.
Using the zeros of sine to find the asymptotes of secant, or the zeros of cosine for cosecant. Secant uses cosine and cosecant uses sine.
Using \(\pi\) as the period of secant or cosecant.

PF2-A-01.hint: Find the excluded values first, then list the ones that fall in the interval by trying \(n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots\) until you leave the interval. Check that the period you found matches the spacing of the asymptotes.
slips: Listing excluded values outside the requested interval.
Dropping the phase shift when listing asymptotes.

Spacing the asymptotes by the period. Tangent and cotangent asymptotes are one period apart, but secant and cosecant asymptotes are only half a period apart, because their period is \(\dfrac{2\pi}{|k|}\) and their asymptotes are \(\dfrac{\pi}{|k|}\) apart.

parts.q: State the domain. Describe the values of \(x\) that must be excluded.
parts.a: The cotangent is undefined where the sine is \(0\), that is where \(2x\) equals \(n\pi\). Solving for \(x\): the domain is all real numbers with \(x \ne \dfrac{n\pi}{2}\), where \(n\) is any integer.
\((-\infty, \infty)\). Stretching or reflecting a tangent or cotangent graph does not change its range.
The period is \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\).

parts.q: State the domain. Describe the values of \(x\) that must be excluded.
parts.a: The tangent is undefined where the cosine is \(0\), that is where \(\dfrac{x}{2}\) equals \(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\). Solving for \(x\): the domain is all real numbers with \(x \ne \pi + 2n\pi\), where \(n\) is any integer.
\((-\infty, \infty)\). Stretching or reflecting a tangent or cotangent graph does not change its range.
The period is \(2\pi\).
